annotation.interpretation_a: A timestamp appearing to be in 2077 (50+ years from 2027) would be interpreted as being in 1977.
annotation.interpretation_b: A timestamp appearing to be in 2051 (more than 50 years from 2001) would be interpreted as being in 1951.
annotation.justification: The phrase 'more than 50 years in the future' is vague. It's unclear whether a timestamp exactly 50 years in the future should be adjusted or not. This leads to different interpretations of the rule for timestamps near the 50-year boundary.
annotation.missing_information: The definition of 'more than 50 years' is not precise. Does it mean strictly greater than 50 years, or greater than or equal to 50 years? This affects the boundary condition and therefore the interpretation of timestamps near the 50-year threshold.
